claims.claim_text: The indexed First Lieutenant Eli Popovich is strongly identified as the engineer whom the official Air Force history documents serving with the OSS in Yugoslavia.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive name, lieutenant rank, engineer description, and explicit OSS Yugoslavia service agree with the index.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence distinctive-name and rank-consistent match in an official military history.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history documents OSS service in 1944; a separate secondary biography supplies the pre-OSS sequence.
claims.match_notes: Ilija (Eli) Popović is retained as a documented name variant from the Serbian-language source.

claims.claim_text: Eli Popovich was an engineer; an official history documents him supervising construction of an airstrip during OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official Air Force history explicitly identifies Popovich as an engineer and describes his airstrip-construction work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence match through exact name, rank, and OSS mission context.
claims.temporal_assessment: Occupation evidence during OSS service; it does not establish a civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: Engineer is published as an occupation, not converted into an employer.

claims.claim_text: A secondary biography reports that Eli Popovich worked in steel mills in several U.S. industrial cities during the 1930s.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The biography places unnamed steel-mill work in the 1930s before Popovich's military and OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence distinctive identity corroborated by the official Air Force history.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar occupation; no mill is named and immediacy is not established.
claims.match_notes: No steel company is inferred; the source also reports Cleveland, Pittsburgh, Detroit, Michigan, and San Pedro without naming firms.

claims.claim_text: A secondary chronology indicates that Eli Popovich's immediate pre-OSS pathway was a U.S. military engineering assignment followed by intelligence training in 1943.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The source places officer training and military-road engineering before an intelligence course and OSS assignment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity; the official Air Force history independently corroborates his engineer occupation and OSS Yugoslavia service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate military assignment from a secondary source; exact unit and transfer date remain unresolved.
claims.match_notes: This is a military assignment, not a civilian employer.

claims.temporal_assessment: The biography explicitly states her status when OSS recruited her.
claims.match_notes: No university is named, so none is inferred.
